To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kinetics of asphaltene thermal decomposition can be used to estimate the temperature conditions of petroleum formation.
the kinetic parameters of petroleum asphaltene thermal breakdown are related to the kinetic parameters of the kerogen thermal breakdown in source rock.

the temperature at the time of formation of petroleum can be estimated from the kinetic properties (activation energy and frequency factor) of petroleum asphaltene, and that this method may be useful in determining the thermal history of petroleum basins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of hydrocarbons formation from petroleum asphalts.
the kinetic properties of the asphaltene fraction of crude oil.
the kinetics of petroleum generation and the relationship between the kinetics of petroleum formation and the kinetics of petroleum asphaltene generation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the kinetics of asphaltene thermal decomposition can provide an independent estimate of the temperature of petroleum generation and can be used to assess the timing of petroleum formation and the extent of available oil reserves in hydrocarbon-bearing basins.
the temperature of the petroleum formation can be determined by measuring the kinetic properties of the asphaltene molecules.
the kinetics of petroleum asphaltene degradation can be used as an alternative method for assessing hydrocarbon potential in petroleum basins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature conditions of petroleum generation can be determined by the kinetic properties of asphaltenic compounds.
the kinetics of petroleum asphal- tenes can be used as a reliable indicator for the temperature conditions of a petroleum source rock during the expulsion process.

the temperature conditions of petroleum formation can be determined from the kinetics of asphaltene breakdown, thus allowing for a more accurate estimation of the petroleum generation characteristics and the available oil resources in a basin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
asphaltenes, as a proxy for the parent kerogen, can be used to predict petroleum formation conditions in the subsurface.
the kinetics of petroleum asphaltene thermal decomposition can be used to estimate the temperature conditions of petroleum formation in source rocks.

the thermal maturation of source rocks can be determined from the kinetic properties (activation energy and frequency factor) of petroleum asphaltene samples, which are more accessible than immature kerogen samples.
